labels.description: Adds recent U.S. federal and state government activities and proposals focused on drivers of childhood chronic diseases, and adds changes in funding for or restrictions on inclusion of the company's products in benefit programs such as SNAP as a demand risk.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: new specific government initiatives and a named program (SNAP) are referenced, which also discloses a new exposure under criterion 1.

labels.description: Adds affordability and consumer spending patterns, perceived undesirability of processed foods, and the reshaping of brand discovery and engagement by data analytics, automation and artificial intelligence on digital platforms as drivers of shifting consumer preferences.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new risk drivers (affordability, spending patterns, AI-driven changes in consumer engagement) are disclosed.

labels.description: Extends the admission of unmet safety standards and past recalls to contract manufacturers, drops the specific reference to value-added dairy and plant-based beverage expansion, broadens recall causes to misbranding, spoilage and undeclared allergens, and adds lost sales from production decreases during remediation and changes in consumer demand as consequences.
labels.rationale: criterion 1 and 2: a new counterparty (contract manufacturers) and new recall causes and consequences are added while the named dairy and plant-based product categories are dropped.

labels.description: Only a page-break position shift and removal of a comma before "or unintentional contaminants"; the text is otherwise identical.
labels.rationale: minor: punctuation and page-number artifact only, with no change in substance.

labels.description: "strong commitment to product safety and quality and human rights" becomes "and respecting human rights", plus a page-break shift.
labels.rationale: minor: stylistic rewording with identical meaning and a page-number artifact.

labels.description: The U.S. alcohol subsidiary's activity is described as producing, distributing and selling alcohol products in the United States, where prior text said producing and selling in certain regions of the United States.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the geographic and operational scope of the U.S. alcohol business is widened from certain regions to the United States and now includes distribution.

labels.description: Adds that one bottler accounted for 10% of net operating revenues for 2025 (reflected in the EMEA and Asia Pacific segments), where no customer concentration figure was given before, and adds the risk that bottlers' actions on quality, safety, marketing, labor, compliance or sustainability could harm the company's brands even if it is not responsible.
labels.rationale: criterion 4 and 1: a new quantitative customer concentration figure (10% of revenue) and a new reputational risk from bottler conduct are disclosed.

labels.description: Only a page number (18) is picked up at the end of the section; the risk factor text is identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-number artifact with no textual change.

labels.description: Only a trailing page number (18) is dropped; the risk factor text is identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-number artifact with no textual change.
